pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📐 **Strand 3 — Geometry And Measurement**
Shape, space, measurement, position and movement — the mathematics of the world around us.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B8.3.1)
- B8.3.1.1 — Demonstrate understanding and use of the relationship between parallel lines and alternate and corresponding angles, and use the sum of angles in a triangle to deduce the angle sum in any polygon.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- identify corresponding, alternate and co-interior (allied) angles formed by a transversal
- find unknown angles using parallel-line facts
- use the angle sum of a triangle (180°) and the exterior angle property
- deduce and use the formula (n − 2) × 180° for the interior angle sum of a polygon

pages.title: Angles formed by parallel lines
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Draw and determine the values of alternate and corresponding angles.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.1.1.1
A **transversal** is a line that crosses two or more other lines. When it crosses two **parallel** lines, eight angles are formed.
[[fig:m8-f22|Figure 8.1: A transversal crossing two parallel lines]]
> 🔑 **Key idea: Parallel-line angle facts** — **Corresponding angles** are equal (in matching positions, an "F" shape): ∠1 = ∠5, ∠2 = ∠6, ∠3 = ∠7, ∠4 = ∠8. **Alternate angles** are equal (on opposite sides of the transversal, between the parallels, a "Z" shape): ∠3 = ∠6, ∠4 = ∠5. **Co-interior (allied) angles** add up to 180° (same side, between the parallels, a "C/U" shape): ∠3 + ∠5 = 180°, ∠4 + ∠6 = 180°.
## ✏️ Example 8.1
In the diagram above, ∠2 = 65°. Calculate the angles marked 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, giving reasons.
**Solution**
At the top intersection, ∠1 and ∠2 lie on a straight line, and ∠3 is vertically opposite ∠2, ∠4 is vertically opposite ∠1:
∠1 = 180° − 65° = **115°** (angles on a straight line)
∠4 = ∠1 = **115°** (vertically opposite)
∠3 = ∠2 = **65°** (vertically opposite)
At the bottom intersection, every angle equals the corresponding angle above:
∠5 = ∠1 = **115°**, ∠6 = ∠2 = **65°**, ∠7 = ∠3 = **65°**, ∠8 = ∠4 = **115°** (corresponding angles)
Check with alternate angles: ∠3 = ∠6 = 65° ✓; co-interior: ∠3 + ∠5 = 65° + 115° = 180° ✓.

pages.title: Example 8.2
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 8.2
Calculate the angles a, b, c and d.
[[fig:m8-f23]]
Figure 8.2: Find a, b, c and d
**Solution**
**a = 72°** (corresponding to the 72° angle)
**b = 108°** (angles on a straight line with a: 180° − 72°)
**c = 72°** (alternate to a — or vertically opposite a)
**d = 108°** (vertically opposite b; also, b and c are co-interior: 108° + 72° = 180°)

pages.title: Angles in triangles and polygons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Determine the values of angles in a triangle using knowledge of the sum of interior angles in a triangle and other properties.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.1.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Angles in a triangle** — The interior angles of any triangle add up to **180°**. An **exterior angle** of a triangle equals the **sum of the two interior opposite angles**.
[[fig:m8-f24|Figure 8.3: Why the angles of a triangle add up to 180°]]
Draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side. The two alternate angles equal the two base angles, and the three angles at the vertex lie on a straight line, so they add up to 180°.
## ✏️ Example 8.3
Calculate y and the angles in the triangle whose angles are y, 2y + 15° and 3y − 15°.
**Solution**
y + (2y + 15) + (3y − 15) = 180 ⟹ 6y = 180 ⟹ **y = 30°**
The angles are **30°, 75° and 75°** (an isosceles triangle).
## Interior angle sum of a polygon
## ✏️ Example 8.4
Deduce the formula for the sum of the interior angles of a polygon and find each interior angle of a regular hexagon.
**Solution**
From one vertex, draw all the diagonals. A polygon with **n** sides is divided into **(n − 2)** triangles, each with angle sum 180°.
[[fig:m8-f25]]
Figure 8.4: Polygons divided into triangles from one vertex
| **Polygon** | **Sides (n)** | **Triangles (n − 2)** | **Angle sum** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Triangle | 3 | 1 | 180° |
| Quadrilateral | 4 | 2 | 360° |
| Pentagon | 5 | 3 | 540° |
| Hexagon | 6 | 4 | 720° |
| Octagon | 8 | 6 | 1,080° |
**Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°**
A regular hexagon has 6 equal angles: 720° ÷ 6 = **120°** each.

pages.title: Example 8.5
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 8.5
Use the formula to find x in the hexagon whose interior angles are 100°, 130°, x, 2x, 140° and 110°.
**Solution**
Sum = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°
100 + 130 + x + 2x + 140 + 110 = 720 ⟹ 3x = 240 ⟹ **x = 80°**
The angles are 100°, 130°, 80°, 160°, 140° and 110°.
> ✨ **Did you know?** The **exterior angles** of any convex polygon (one at each vertex) add up to **360°**. So each exterior angle of a regular n-gon is 360° ÷ n, and each interior angle is 180° minus that.

pages.title: Exercise 8.2
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 8.2** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Find the third angle of a triangle whose other angles are: a) 47° and 68° b) 90° and 35.5°
2. The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find them.
3. An exterior angle of a triangle is 125°. One interior opposite angle is 70°. Find the other.
4. Find the interior angle sum of: a) a heptagon (7 sides) b) a decagon (10 sides) c) a 15-sided polygon
5. Find each interior angle of a regular: a) pentagon b) octagon c) 12-sided polygon
6. The interior angles of a pentagon are x, x + 20°, x + 40°, x + 60° and x + 80°. Find x.
7. Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 144°. How many sides does it have?

pages.title: Chapter 8 summary
pages.body:
- Corresponding angles are equal; alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add up to 180°.
- Angles in a triangle add up to 180°; an exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.
- Interior angle sum of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°; exterior angles add up to 360°.
